CPRADDENDA.settings.enforceWeaponTypes.h: An upgrade with a weapon type list only fits matching weapons. A silencer will not screw onto a shotgun, a sniper drum magazine will not fit a pistol. Upgrades without a list behave exactly as before.
CPRADDENDA.settings.installedUsage.name: Upgrade effects with 'while installed' mode
CPRADDENDA.settings.installedUsage.hint: Restores the 'Installed' option to the effect usage list. An upgrade's effect then lasts exactly as long as the upgrade stays in the item. The system supports this mode but only offers it for cyberware.
CPRADDENDA.settings.showSheetControls.na: Show helper rows on item sheets
CPRADDENDA.settings.showSheetControls.hi: Adds 'Installs into' and 'Weapon Types' rows to upgrade sheets, and an 'Accepts upgrades' toggle to carrier items — the one the system does not expose.
CPRADDENDA.notify.wrongWeaponType: "{upgrade}" does not fit "{weapon}": that is a {type}. Fits: {allowed}.
CPRADDENDA.notify.deniedWeaponType: "{upgrade}" does not fit "{weapon}": the type "{type}" is excluded.
CPRADDENDA.dialog.title: {name}: which weapons accept it
CPRADDENDA.dialog.hint: Tick the weapon types. With nothing ticked there is no restriction and the upgrade fits any weapon.
CPRADDENDA.carrier.acceptsHint: Allow upgrades to be installed into this item. If it has no slots, three are opened.
CPRADDENDA.carrier.overlap: "{upgrade}" changes the same fields on "{item}" as another installed upgrade. Remove them in reverse order, or the values will not restore correctly.
CPRADDENDA.dv.hintBody: The module ships an extended set of DV-by-range tables: short and long barrels, carbine, battle/marksman/scout/heavy sniper rifles, bows with different limbs. Without them barrel modifications cannot change range — the system reads tables from a single compendium only.
CPRADDENDA.dv.hintWhere: If the button did not help, close Foundry entirely and start it again: new compendiums register only at server start.
CPRADDENDA.dv.hintSafety: Switching is safe: the pack also contains every table under its system name, so stock weapons keep their tables.
CPRADDENDA.dv.switched: Done: the system now reads DV tables from the module's pack ({count} tables).
CPRADDENDA.dv.packMissing: The module's table pack was not found. Close Foundry completely and start it again — new compendiums are only picked up when the server starts; reloading the page is not enough.
CPRADDENDA.dv.switchFailed: Could not change the setting, see the console (F12).
CPRADDENDA.settings.aimedShotPatch.name: Replace the aimed shot penalty
CPRADDENDA.settings.aimedShotPatch.hint: Lets targeting upgrades (Superscanner) replace the system's −8 penalty with their own value. This is the only place the module touches a roll — turn it off if you suspect a conflict with other modules.
CPRADDENDA.dv.restored: The system DV table compendium has been restored.

pkt.failed: {frame}: could not deploy the kit. See the console (F12) for details.

CPRADDENDA.vehicle.position.name: Position Name
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.position.matchVehicle: Match Occupant MOVE to Vehicle MOVE
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.position.matchOccupan: Match Vehicle MOVE to Occupant MOVE
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.crew.eject: Remove from Vehicle and delete the effect
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.upgrades.title: Vehicle Upgrades
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.cargo.title: Cargo & Equipment
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.damage.title: Critical Injuries
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.empty.dragUpgrades: Drag vehicle upgrades from the Cargo tab
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.glass.title: {position}: bulletproof glass
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.noWeaponPositi: No weapon-capable positions found. Tick “Can Control Weapons” in a position's settings.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.oldModuleActiv: The module “MMuton's CPR Vehicle Actor Sheet” is still enabled. The vehicle sheet now lives in Cyberpunk RED: Addenda — disable the old module, or position effects will be applied twice.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.migration.done: Vehicle data migrated: {actors} actors, {items} items, {effects} effects, {armor} armor plates, {fixes} system-data corrections, {effectFlags} repaired effects.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.migration.failed: Vehicle data migration did not finish — see the console (F12). It will be retried on the next world load.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.settings.keepGmPermis: While enabled, the vehicle sheet only raises a player's permissions when they board and clears them when they leave, never lowering what the GM granted by hand. Disable to let the sheet manage permissions entirely.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.weaponNotMount: “{name}” is not mounted to any position. Click the chain icon next to it and pick a position.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.postGone: The position “{name}” was mounted to no longer exists. Mount the weapon again.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.postEmpty: Nobody is at the “{position}” position. Drag an actor onto it — the occupant rolls, not the vehicle.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.gunnerGone: The actor seated at “{position}” was not found. Remove and seat them again.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.notify.noWeaponSkill: “{actor}” has no “{skill}” skill, which “{name}” requires. The system matches the skill by its exact English name — add it to the character sheet.
CPRADDENDA.settings.importCorebook.name: Put the rulebook into the world
CPRADDENDA.settings.importCorebook.hint: Source page links only search world journals — they never look inside compendiums. While this is on, the module adds the rulebook to the world once, on load, if it is not there yet. Turn it off if you bring the book in by hand.
CPRADDENDA.corebook.imported: The rulebook was added to the world — source page links now work.
CPRADDENDA.corebook.alreadyHere: The rulebook is already in this world: “{journal}”. Nothing was added.
CPRADDENDA.corebook.failed: Could not add the rulebook to the world — see the console (F12).
CPRADDENDA.corebook.needPdfPager: Source page links will not work: the PDF Pager module is not enabled. Enable it in module management — it renders the PDF and resolves the page code.
CPRADDENDA.settings.explosiveTemplates.h: When a rocket or grenade launcher is fired from a vehicle position, the module places a 5 × 5 square area on the target and posts the Explosives rule to chat. Damage and dodges are not rolled automatically: where a miss lands is the GM's call, and dodging is the player's choice.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.title: blast area {squares} × {squares} squares ({size} × {size} {units})
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.damageOnce: Damage is rolled once and applied to every target in the area, environment included. Armor reduces it as usual.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.dodge: Anyone in the area with REF 8 or higher may try to dodge: their roll must beat {total}. On a success they move out of the area.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.miss: If the roll fell short of the DV to hit the target, the GM decides where inside this square the blast actually went off and moves the area there.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.noTarget: No target selected, so there is nowhere to place the blast area for “{name}”. Target a token (press T over it) and fire again.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.failed: The blast area was not placed: {message}
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.applyHint: In the damage card each target has its own ⚡ button — apply the damage one by one. Skip anyone who dodged. The button at the top of the card hits the tokens currently selected on the canvas, not the targets.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.dodgeSuccess: {name} dodges: {result} against {total}. Moved clear of the area, no damage.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.dodgeFail: {name} fails to dodge: {result} against {total}. Stays in the area and takes the blast damage.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.noEvasion: {name} has no Evasion skill, so there is nothing to roll. Add the skill to the sheet.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.dodgeNotYours: {name} is not your character. Their player or the GM rolls the dodge.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.damageNotYours: Blast damage is rolled by whoever fired, or by the GM.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.weaponGone: The weapon from this shot can no longer be found — it was deleted or the world changed. Fire again.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.blast.tokenGone: That token is no longer on the scene, so there is nobody to dodge.
CPRADDENDA.vehicle.migration.armorText:
Power armor plating: SP {sp}.

Added during a module update: the SP used to live only in the sheet header and was never subtracted when damage was applied.
CPRADDENDA.settings.systemFixes.name: Correct mismatches in the system's own data
CPRADDENDA.settings.systemFixes.hint: A few compendium items disagree with their own description and with the book: MultiOptic Mount and Sensor Array have three slots instead of five, and the Fūma Kotarō frame is missing its Stealth bonus. The correction is applied when the item is added to a sheet.
CPRADDENDA.fixes.multiOptic.applied: {name}: slots raised to 5, as its description and Data Pool state; the compendium had 3.
CPRADDENDA.fixes.sensorArray.applied: {name}: slots raised to 5, as its description and Data Pool state; the compendium had 3.
CPRADDENDA.fixes.fumaStealth.applied: {name}: added the +2 Stealth bonus the frame grants; the compendium was missing it.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.title: Installing Full Body Conversion: {name}
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.confirm.lead: You are about to install the Full Body Conversion frame {name}. This is permanent: the meat body stays on the table.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.confirm.warn: The frame requires an installed Biosystem. The module does not check for it — that call is the GM's.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.free.lead: These implants come with the frame and cost no Humanity:
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.free.note: By the FBC rules, cyberarms, cyberaudio, cybereyes, cyberlegs, cyberskull, linear frame and neural link deal 0 loss and do not reduce the Humanity recoverable through therapy.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.cost.lead: These implants come with Humanity loss. Here is where each one goes:
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.cost.humanity: Humanity loss for the whole kit: {formula}, average — {average}.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.cost.choose: The FBC rules allow taking the average instead of rolling. Choose how to count it.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.summary.lead: The {name} frame is ready to install. Summary:
CPRADDENDA.pkt.cancelled: Installation of “{frame}” cancelled; the frame was removed from the sheet.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.cyberpsycho: Humanity dropped to zero or below — by the rules that is cyberpsychosis.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.nothingDeployed: The “{name}” frame was installed, but none of its kit implants appeared. Check the console (F12): this is a bug, not a design choice.
CPRADDENDA.pkt.wizard.mookNote: This is an NPC. Cyberpunk RED does not track Humanity for NPCs, but the system still derives EMP from it — fifty-odd points for a frame will push the NPC into the negative. Mooks usually take “no loss”.
CPRADDENDA.settings.mookEmpathy.name: Keep the EMP you typed on NPCs when installing cyberware
CPRADDENDA.settings.mookEmpathy.hint: The system derives EMP from Humanity on every install, and derives Humanity from EMP max — a field the mook sheet does not expose. So the first implant overwrites whatever EMP the GM typed. Cyberpunk RED does not track Humanity for NPCs, so their EMP is restored to the typed value. Player characters are unaffected.
